# neuron v0.1.0 — public beta mk1

first public build of neuron: a control layer for razer mice and keyboards, replacing synapse.
one person, one desk, and until now the only eyes and hands on this were mine. this is the point
where that changes. windows x86_64 only.

nothing here is a promise. where every feature actually stands, solid to barely-started, is
tracked in [state of the project](https://github.com/worflor/neuron/blob/main/docs/STATUS.md) and stays current after this tag; these notes
are a snapshot.

## before you run it

- **windows 10/11, x86_64.** no linux/mac build yet — the seams are there in the code, the
  backends aren't written.
- **the zip is not code-signed.** windows SmartScreen will warn on first run — *more info → run
  anyway*. instead of a signature, this release carries a **build provenance attestation**: proof,
  signed by GitHub, that the zip came from this exact commit and workflow run. verify it instead
  of trusting a publisher name:

  ```
  gh attestation verify neuron-v0.1.0-windows-x86_64.zip --repo worflor/neuron
  ```

  `SHA256SUMS.txt` is attached to this release too, if you just want a checksum match.
- **close synapse first.** razer's driver mode is a lease — whichever host flips it last owns the
  device's live control state. neuron and synapse fighting over the same device at once isn't a
  supported setup; run one or the other. if you're leaving synapse for good, neuron can purge it.
- **elevation isn't required to run neuron**, but the native Chroma shared-memory face (the thing
  that lets games talk to your lighting the same way they'd talk to Razer's own service) needs
  `SeCreateGlobalPrivilege` to create its `Global\` objects. without it, that face falls back to
  REST-only. to get it, turn on start-with-windows (below): that launches neuron elevated at
  every logon.

## getting started

1. extract the zip anywhere writable.
2. run `neuron-app.exe`. `neuron.exe` is the CLI, same engine, same config.
3. **where config lives**: for a zip install, both binaries resolve every runtime path against
   the folder the exe sits in — copy the folder, keep your setup, no registry, no AppData
   scatter. (only a from-source build run straight out of `target\release` uses
   `%LOCALAPPDATA%\neuron` instead, so a `cargo clean` can't take your config with it.) set
   `NEURON_RUN_DIR` if you want it somewhere else.
4. **autostart is off by default.** nothing registers itself on first launch. to turn it on,
   run `neuron-app.exe` **as administrator** once (right-click → run as administrator), then
   flip "start with windows" on the SYSTEM page. it's a scheduled task, "Neuron (elevated tray)",
   rather than a registry Run key, and registering an elevated task needs an elevated caller.
   from then on it starts elevated at logon by itself. flipping the toggle off removes the logon
   trigger but keeps the task, so you can still launch it elevated on demand.

## what works

per [state of the project](https://github.com/worflor/neuron/blob/main/docs/STATUS.md):

**solid — lean on it.**
device control (dpi, polling, brightness, battery, reads, side-plate, scroll stage), the
trigger → action spine (binds, hypershift, app-focus), the arm gate, audio control (mute / gain /
output-flip), synapse import / purge / discover, notifications.

**works, still polishing.**
profiles (capture · apply · rename · auto-switch by app — just had a proper pass, treat the edges
as freshly-fixed), capability-driven device support (any `razer_report` device should adopt
itself; two are hardware-verified — Naga V2 Pro and BlackWidow Chroma V2 — other families are a
per-family seam), the lighting engine (pattern × spectrum, positionable data layers), macros &
beacons (warm CPython sidecar, ask/notify, a persistent KV store, macro-calls-macro), GUI
rendering (GPU now, via femtovg, with a software fallback), general UI polish.

**rough / under-tested — expect edges.**
reliability & recovery (flight recorder + crash log + diagnostics bench are wired; the
auto-relaunch on crash/hang has never actually had to fire), on-device/onboard memory (storage
accounting and volatile writes work, full onboard profile-slot persistence doesn't), spellweaving
at scale (the recognition engine is solid, a big glyph vault + full radial hasn't been lived in),
the instrument suite (teleport, tether, whiteboard, glance, window verbs, dial, knockback,
control — present, uneven, the whiteboard can't save its ink yet), the CLI (a full command
surface, less driven day to day than the GUI), integrations via neuron-host (Chroma + OpenRGB
pipes work, the control surface and teardown guarantees are still being hardened), momentary
mic/push-to-talk (wired end to end, light mileage).

**not built yet.**
richer interpretation + dynamic redraw for integrations, linux/mac backends.

## what doesn't, yet

- **device write honesty ledger** (from the README):
  - **gated behind a feature flag until a capture confirms them**: in-game hi-res polling,
    scroll *stage* table, snap-tap (SOCD) — payloads are unit-tested and read-back-verified
    already, they're just not flipped on.
  - **no known opcode, refuses rather than guessing**: debounce, saving a button remap into
    onboard memory.
  - **doesn't crack synapse's encrypted cloud profiles** — migration reads the plaintext export,
    not the AES'd account cache.
  - **doesn't sandbox macros.** full, unsandboxed CPython. the arm gate guards the convenience
    helpers, not the raw APIs underneath.
  - no telemetry, no account, no cloud — none of that is coming later either, it's a non-goal.

## safe by default

- the arm gate starts **disarmed**: no synthesized keystroke, click, or process-spawn goes out
  until you deliberately arm it. reads are always safe regardless.
- device writes are volatile (`NOSTORE`) unless you ask otherwise. the one exception is
  `neuron scroll <stage>`, which stores onboard by default like synapse (`--volatile` opts out).
  every write is re-read against the matching getter to
  confirm the bytes actually landed — a mismatch is a hard error, never a silent success.
- `neuron run --safe` runs the whole engine — triggers resolve, actions get logged — with real
  input synthesis held disarmed, so you can watch what would happen before it happens.

## reporting problems

open an issue with the [bug report template](https://github.com/worflor/neuron/issues/new?template=bug_report.md): device + PID,
windows build, what happened, how to reproduce. if it's device- or lighting-shaped, the SYSTEM
page has a diagnostics bench — nine read-only probes, always safe, never writes to your hardware —
run it and paste the output. attach `neuron-crash.log` from your run root if there is one.

## uninstalling

1. quit neuron from the tray.
2. if you ever turned on "start with windows", delete its scheduled task. turning the toggle
   off isn't enough, because that keeps the task. from a terminal run as administrator:

   ```
   schtasks /delete /tn "Neuron (elevated tray)" /f
   ```

3. delete the folder you extracted the zip into. for a zip install that's your binaries and
   your config together, since both resolve against that folder.
4. if you set `NEURON_RUN_DIR` somewhere else, delete that folder too.
5. if you ever built from source and ran it out of `target\release`, also check
   `%LOCALAPPDATA%\neuron`. that's where that config lived.

that's the whole footprint: no installer, no service, no registry entries, and the one
scheduled task from step 2 if you enabled autostart.
